runs.text: OLD TESTAMENT:
1. What moved upon the face of the waters?
Genesis 1:2
And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep.
And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
Note
: The term Spirit of God is from the Hebrew word “
ruwach
roo’-akh
). The term is referring to the Spirit of God.
It is interesting to note that the Hebrew word “
ruwach
” is interpreted as wind 92 times, and breath 27 times in the Old Testament.
2. What came upon David?
1 Samuel 16:13
Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren:
and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward.
Note:

The Spirit of the Lord came upon David. This is the same Hebrew word as in the last question. This means that the “breath” of God came upon David. But also notice that this experience was upon David from that day forward. What this means is that the Spirit of God has to be more than just the breath of God. It must include God’s presence.
3. What was put upon God’s prophets?
Numbers 11:29
And Moses said unto him… Would God that all the LORD’S people were prophets,
and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!
Note:
In the Old Testament God’s Spirit was often placed upon people for specific purposes.
Judges 6:34 Spirit came on Gideon.
Judges 14:6 Spirit enables Samson.
1 Samuel 16:13-14 Spirit came upon David.
Isaiah 59:21 Spirit was upon Isaiah.
THE NEW COVENANT CHANGE:
4. Where would God put His Spirit?
Ezekiel 36:27
And I will put my spirit within you
, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.
Note:

In the New Covenant, God would dwell "within them." This is a different manifestation than the Old Testament experience of having the Spirit in or upon them for a specific purpose. This is part of the New Covenant promise. In the future, God would dwell within them and cause them to walk in His statutes. Prior to this, the Spirit would come to guide, inspire, and aid. Now He would tabernacle (dwell) in them and change their hard hearts to walk in His statutes. (See Ezekiel 11:19-20)
NEW TESTAMENT:
5. Does the Holy Spirit now dwell in the believer?
1 Corinthians 3:16
Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you
Note:
If you are a believer, then the Bible calls you God's temple because “
the Spirit of God dwelleth in you
”. The Holy Spirit controls the believer who believes in Christ and submits himself to God's will.
6. Can the unbeliever receive the things of the Spirit?
1 Corinthians 2:14
But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God
: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.
Note:
The Holy Spirit does not indwell the unbeliever, but the Bible shows that the Holy Spirit does make contact with, to influence, and to affect the life of the unbeliever. (See John 16: 8-11)
WHO IS THE SPIRIT THAT INDWELLS?
7. Who is the Holy Spirit?
2 Corinthians 3:17
Now the Lord is that Spirit
: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
Note:
The Lord is that Spirit. Many have been reading this text for years but only realize what it is saying after someone points it out to them. Christ is that Spirit.
8. Who feeds the church of God?
Acts 20:28
Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the
which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood
Note:

Once you see this truth you can’t unsee it. Are you beginning to notice that the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of Christ? The Spirit purchased the church with His own blood. It was Christ’s blood that purchased the church.
9. What was the last Adam made?
1 Corinthians 15:45
And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul;
the last Adam was made a quickening spirit.
Note:
The second Adam is the Spirit of Christ. Christ was made a quickening Spirit.
10. Who groaned in the spirit?
John 11:33
When Jesus
therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her,
he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled
11. Who was the Spirit that was groaning in verse 33?
John 11:38
Jesus therefore again groaning in himself
cometh to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
Note

: Many assume that it was a third god called god the holy spirit who was groaning in verse 33. But verse 38 tells us that Jesus was groaning in himself. The Bible never calls the Holy Spirit “God the Holy Spirit”! The language that the scripture uses when referring to the Holy Spirit is: “The Spirit of Christ”! (See Romans 8:9, 1 Peter 1:11)
THE COMFORTER:
12. Who is it that gives us comfort?
John 14:18
I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more; but ye see me: because I live, ye shall live also. At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me,
and I in you
Note:
The word “comforter” is derived from the Greek word
parakletos
Parakleto
s is only used five times in the entire Bible.
In four of the verses
parakletos
is interpreted as “comforter”, and in the fifth verse as “advocate”.
Let’s see what we can learn about the five verses that tell us about the comforter from the Apostle John.
13. Who is the Comforter?
John 14:26
But the Comforter, [parakletos] which is the Holy Ghost
, whom the Father will send in my name.
Note:
John 14:26 tells us that the comforter is the Holy Ghost.
14. Where does the Spirit of truth come from?
John 15:26
But when the Comforter [parakletos] is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me.
Note:
John 15:26 tells us that the comforter is the Spirit of Truth. This verse also tells us that the comforter “proceedeth from the Father”.
15. Who sends the Comforter?
John 16:7
Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter [parakletos] will not come unto you; but if I depart,
I will send
him
unto you
Note:

John 15:26, 16:7 tells us that Jesus sends the comforter from the Father. Who is this comforter? It is Christ in His omnipresent Spirit form. The latter part of this verse says I will send “him” unto you. The word “him” can also be interpreted as “it”, or “itself”. It can also be interpreted as “the same”. In other words, Jesus would send someone “the same” as himself to them. It is interesting to note that the Greek word “
autos
” is interpreted as “himself” 58 times in the New Testament.

So, what this means is that after Jesus went away to heaven, He sent “Himself” in the form of His omnipresent Spirit back to His disciples. When you have this correct understanding, all the pieces of this puzzle fit together.
16. Who is the Comforter (advocate /
parakletos
1 John 2:1
My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin,
we have an advocate [parakletos] with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.
Note:
1 John 2:1 tells us exactly who the
parakletos
is: “
Jesus Christ the righteous
What do we learn from this? We learn that the comforter
[parakletos]
is the Spirit of Christ. The comforter is not a different third god, named God the Holy Spirit as many suppose.
This brings us back to John 14:18 (
Question #12
). Jesus tells His disciples that He will not leave them comfortless, that “
He
” will come unto them! John 14:18
“I will not leave you comfortless:
I will come to you
ANOTHER COMFORTER:
17. Doesn’t John 14:16 say, “another” comforter?
John 14:16
And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter
[parakletos], that he may abide with you for ever.
Note:
Doesn’t this mean that Jesus will send a different comforter as many suppose?

The Greek language is much more expressive than the English language. For example: English has only one word to describe “love”, but the Greek language has four different Greek words to describe “love”. This is also true of the word “another”. The Greek language has two different Greek words to describe the English word “another”. John used both of these Greek words in the book of John. He used the Greek word “
allos
” [243] in John 14:16 and then in John 19:37 he used the Greek word “
Heteros
” [2087]. So John was certainly aware that two different Greek words were available to him to describe the comforter.
Allos
” [243] = one of the same kind.
Heteros
” [2087] = one of a different kind.
John used the word, “
allos

” to describe “another comforter”! He was describing one of the same kind. What this means is that John could have used a different word to describe a comforter of a different kind than Christ. But he did not use the word “
heteros
”. He used the word “
allos,
” because Jesus is sending His own spirit, not the spirit of another kind.
This is really good news! Only Christ was tempted as we are, only Christ understands the feelings of our infirmities, and only He can help (
Succour
) and understand us in our time of need. (See Hebrews 2:18)
18. Why does Christ feel the feelings of our infirmities?
Hebrews 4:15
For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
Note:

Christ sends His own spirit and He says His Spirit will abide with us forever! (See John 14:16) The fact that Christ sends His own Spirit is much better news than if He had sent a different spirit than Himself. Jesus feels the feelings of our infirmities (See Hebrews 4:15) and only Christ is able to
succour
us in our time of need. (See Hebrews 2:18) As the son of man Jesus understands us.
19. Whose Spirit does God send into our hearts?
Galatians 4:6
And because ye are sons,
God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
Note:
God sends the Spirit of His Son. The Bible never calls the Holy Spirit, “God the Holy Spirit”! The Bible always says it is the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of Christ!
FROM THE FATHER THROUGH THE SON:
20. From whom does Jesus get His Spirit that He sheds?
Acts 2:32
This Jesus hath God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses. Therefore being by the right hand of God exalted, and
having received of the Father the promise of the Holy Ghost, he hath shed forth this, which ye now see and hear.
Note:
In the New Testament, the Holy Spirit dwells in the believer. The Spirit comes from the Father, to Christ, and then is shed forth into our hearts.
21. Whose Spirit dwelt in the Apostle Paul?
Philippians 1:19
For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
Note:
The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of Christ. Jesus received this Spirit from His Father.
22. Whose Spirit spoke to the church of Thyatira?
Revelation 2: 18, 29
And unto the angel of the church in Thyatira write;
These things saith the
son of God
… He that hath an ear, let him hear
what the
Spirit
saith unto the churches.
Note:
We are starting to see this picture more clearly. Next we will look at the Spirit and the latter rain.
HOLY SPIRIT POURED OUT IN THE LATTER RAIN:
23. Who is sent when the time of refreshing comes?
Acts 3:19
Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out,
when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;
And he shall send Jesus Christ
which before was preached unto you.
24. Who shall come unto us as the latter rain?
Hosea 6:3
Then shall we know,
if we follow on to know the LORD: his going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.
Note:

There are two outpourings of the Spirit of Christ. These are called the former and latter rain. The first outpouring was at Pentecost. The second outpouring is promised to ripen the grain for harvest at the end of time.
25. What happens when God pours the latter rain?
Joel 2:23
Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God: for
he hath given you the former rain moderately,
and he will cause to come down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month. …28
And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:
And also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit.
30 And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke. 31 The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood,
before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come
Note:

The former rain was an outpouring of the Holy Spirit of Christ at Pentecost. The latter rain comes at the end of time before the great and terrible day of the Lord. When this happens “your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions.”

In Israel there were two rains. The early rain was the rain that came with the sowing of the grain. Then as the grain began to ripen, the latter rain fell, ripening the fruit of the grain for harvest. Likewise, the gospel seed was sown in the first century church, then before Christ returns, the latter rain is poured out in more abundance than the former rain. This happens before the great and terrible day of the Lord. The great and terrible day of the Lord is the second coming of Christ.
26. What are we to ask for?
Zechariah 10:1
Ask ye of the LORD rain in the time of the latter rain;
so the LORD shall make bright clouds, and give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field. 2
For the idols have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie, and have told false dreams;
they comfort in vain: therefore they went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd.
Note:

We are admonished to ask for an outpouring of the Spirit of Christ in the time of the latter rain. The conditions of the church during this time is a time of subtle idolatry. There are lies being told at this time. There are false dreams and false doctrines being promoted. It is for this reason that we need the Spirit of Christ poured out. And like Elijah, your young men will receive visions to see the truth about the prevailing idolatry.
27. What must we do before the latter rain?
Hosea 6:1
Come, and
let us return unto the LORD
for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up
. 2 After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. 3
Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the LORD: his going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us
as the rain, as the latter and former rain
unto the earth.
O Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away
. 5 Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth:
and thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth.
Note:

Ephraim and Judah were involved in idolatry. (See Hosea 4:17) We are to pray for rain and pray for visions to learn the truth in the time of the latter rain. But the rain will not fall on us until we return to the Lord. There will be judgments falling in the time of the latter rain. These judgments have a purpose. These judgments are the light that goes forth. They are calling us to repent and
return to the Lord
28. What will be removed from those who repent?
Hosea 2:16
And it shall be at that day, saith the LORD, that thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali. 17
For I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth, and they shall no more be remembered by their name.
Note:

Idolatry has crept back into God’s church at the end of time, and like the days of Elijah, the church can not see her condition. (See 1 Kings 18:21, Revelation 3:17) But many at the end will repent of this “foul spirit”. (See Revelation 18:2,4) When the final generation repents and returns to the Lord, they will then call God Ishi (husband) and no more Baali.
IDOLATRY TODAY:

The current mainstream teaching in Christianity is that God is a co-equal, co-eternal, one-substance, three in one God, and that Jesus Christ is also God almighty. This doctrine is considered by many as the cornerstone of Christianity, but where did this doctrine come from? The historical record is overwhelming that the church of the first three centuries did not worship God as a co-equal, co-eternal, consubstantial, one-substance three in one mysterious godhead. The early church worshiped One God and believed in a divine, but subordinate Son. The idea of a three in one god originated with Babylon, and was passed on to most of the world's religions. Polytheistic trinitarianism (believing in more than one god) was intertwined with Greek religion and philosophy, and slowly worked its way into Christian thought and creeds some 300 years after Christ. Reference: Wikipedia)

The Bible teaches that Jesus is the “son of God”! The idea of "God the Son" is from Babylonian mythology which was grafted into Christianity in the fourth century. God condemns idolatry, even when it is in its most subtle form. (See 1 Kings 18:21) (See Tract # 12, “
Babylon

The Bible refers to Jesus as the Son of God over 50 times; it never refers to him as God the Son in a trinitarian sense. The phrase Son of God is in the genitive case; showing that Jesus originated from, and belongs to God. In no way can the Son of God be the same as God the Son. This violates grammar, language, and common sense. God the Son is not a Biblical term, it does not appear in the Greek, Hebrew, or Aramaic texts. God the Son is a Babylonian term. The Babylonians made Nimrod a god, and when he died they deified his son Tammuz as God the Son. This false belief was carried into almost all pagan religions, and eventually worked its way into Christianity.
29. Whom did Jesus send to His disciples?
John 14:18
I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.

When Jesus went back to heaven, He retained His humanity and could not be present in heaven and be present with His disciples at the same time. So He sent His independent omnipresent Spirit back to His disciples. He promised them that He would never leave them or forsake them. He said, I will not leave you comfortless, “I will come unto you”. The Holy Spirit is Christ returning in a way that’s not bound by physical limits.
We are not advocating Unitarianism, Oneness-Pentecostalism, Jesus-Only, J-W, or Modalism!

There is one God, the literal Father, and He has a literal, divine, yet subordinate son. The Holy Spirit is their Spirit. The Holy Spirit operates independently of the Father and Son, but it is not a third non-Biblical, unknown god called God the Holy Spirit! The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of the Father and the Son.

At the end of the day, traditional Trinitarianism, Unitarianism, Oneness-Pentecostalism, etc. are also heresies because they do not present a literal Father who gave His real, literal, begotten son. Both Modalist and Trinitarians admit this, stating that the terms begotten and son are only metaphors and are not literal. (See
trinities.org
metaphor
) (See Tract #11, “
Son of God
God sent His real Son, not a metaphor!
John 3:36
He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life.
